full_text_en:
Tie Ying Bribery Case

Defendant: Tie Ying, female, 66 years old, of Shandong Province, former Deputy Director of the Standing Committee of the Beijing Municipal People's Congress. She was arrested in connection with this case on February 8, 1996, and released on bail pending trial on June 24, 1997.

The Branch Procuratorate of the Beijing Municipal People's Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution against defendant Tie Ying for bribery, and brought the case before the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court.

The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court conducted a public trial of this case in accordance with the law. The following facts were found:

During the period from 1992 to 1995, while successively serving as Secretary General of the Beijing Municipal People's Government and concurrently Director of the Municipal Government's Legal Affairs Office, Director of the Municipal Government's General Office, and Deputy Director of the Standing Committee of the Beijing Municipal People's Congress, defendant Tie Ying took advantage of her official position to seek benefits for others and accepted huge amounts of property given to her by others, as follows:

1. In November and December 1992, when defendant Tie Ying served as Deputy Head and concurrently Secretary General of the Beijing Municipal People's Government Delegation to the Beijing Investment and Trade Fair in Hong Kong to attract investment, she accepted from Hong Kong businessman Liu Changming: one pair of ROLEX President men's and women's watches (valued at a total of RMB 152,700), one SONY CCD-TR303E video camera (valued at RMB 8,800), and three gold necklaces (valued at RMB 2,060). After returning to Beijing, Tie Ying accepted the request of Liu Changming to provide assistance in negotiating a joint venture project between Liu and the Beijing Xindadu Industrial General Company, a subsidiary of the Beijing Municipal People's Government, and participated in approving three joint venture projects. The joint venture projects were later cancelled due to reasons such as the Hong Kong businessman's failure to provide the required capital.

2. In 1992, defendant Tie Ying, because she had accepted the request of Li Lu, Chairman of the Board of Tianping Liyuan Hotel Co., Ltd., and Liang Bing, its consultant, and had helped resolve the issue of the company's payment of land use right transfer fees, accepted from Li Lu one SONY VF1 desktop stereo system (valued at RMB 10,800).

3. In 1992 and 1993, defendant Tie Ying, because she had provided support and assistance to the Xindadu Hotel under her supervision in matters such as loans, expansion, and introduction of joint ventures, accepted on three occasions from Shi Luming (separately dealt with), General Manager of the Xindadu Hotel, a total of HKD 20,000 (equivalent to approximately RMB 14,400), RMB 10,000, and one sapphire ring and one jade ring (valued at RMB 3,890).

4. In 1992 and 1993, defendant Tie Ying accepted the request of Taiwan businessman Wu Changming to coordinate and resolve a dispute between Wu Changming and others and the Yuanshan Hotel, a subsidiary of the Beijing Agriculture, Industry and Commerce General Company, and helped Wu Changming apply for a low-interest loan of RMB 2,000,000 from the Beijing Municipal Fiscal Fund Management Sub-bureau. On three occasions, she accepted from Wu Changming one diamond ring (valued at over RMB 42,000), one OMEGA women's watch (valued at RMB 6,300), and USD 10,000 (equivalent to approximately RMB 57,600).

5. In October 1993, defendant Tie Ying accepted the request of Yang Yongjian, Deputy General Manager of Shandong Xinmu Group Company, to help the Group Company raise funds. After Tie Ying contacted the Beijing Jinghua Trust and Investment Company, the company purchased 10,000,000 shares (at RMB 1 per share) of Xinmu Steel Co., Ltd. stock. Tie Ying therefore accepted RMB 5,000 from Yang Yongjian, Deputy General Manager of Shandong Xinmu International Group Company.

6. In March 1994, while visiting Hong Kong, defendant Tie Ying, because she had previously helped Hong Kong businessman Luo Zhuo establish "Tongrentang Yushan Co., Ltd." as a joint venture in Hong Kong with the Beijing Medicinal Materials Company and Beijing Tongrentang No. 2 Pharmaceutical Factory, accepted from Luo Zhuo HKD 50,000 (equivalent to approximately RMB 56,300).

7. In March 1994, while visiting Hong Kong, defendant Tie Ying, because she had previously accepted the request of Hong Kong businessman Huang Zhali to help establish "Beijing Xianlong International Garden Co., Ltd." as a joint venture with Miyun County and "Beijing Xijingyuan Funeral Service Co., Ltd." as a joint venture with the Funeral Administration Office of the Beijing Municipal Civil Affairs Bureau, accepted from Huang Zhali one gold Buddha statue (valued at RMB 15,808) and one thousand-Buddha-eye gold note (valued at RMB 2,444).

8. In 1995, defendant Tie Ying, because she had accepted the request of Hong Kong businessman Li Guancheng to help resolve matters concerning the approval of joint venture projects for Beijing Shengyin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., accepted from Li Guancheng one ROLEX women's watch (valued at RMB 42,000).

The above facts are confirmed by the testimonies of witnesses Huang Jicheng, Wu Changming, Yang Yongjian, Luo Zhuo, Huang Zhali, Li Guancheng, and others; documentary evidence such as the joint venture project report between Beijing Xindadu Industrial General Company and Hong Kong China Feida (Group) Co., Ltd., the approval form of the Beijing Municipal People's Government, and the appraisal report of stolen goods from the Beijing Price Office; and the stolen goods seized and produced in court. Defendant Tie Ying also confessed to the facts.

In summary, defendant Tie Ying accepted bribes totaling over RMB 430,000 in money and property. All the bribe money and goods have been recovered in the case.

The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held: The facts charged by the Branch Procuratorate of the Beijing Municipal People's Procuratorate that defendant Tie Ying committed the crime of bribery are clear, and the evidence is reliable and sufficient. Tie Ying, being a state functionary, took advantage of her official position to accept huge amounts of property from others in exchange for seeking benefits for them. Pursuant to Article 4, Paragraph 1 of the Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Punishing Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery (hereinafter referred to as the "Supplementary Provisions"), her conduct constitutes the crime of bribery, and the circumstances of her crime are serious. In view of the fact that Tie Ying truthfully confessed the facts of her crime during the trial, exposed and reported the crimes of others, demonstrated genuine repentance and meritorious service, and that all bribe money and goods have been recovered, a relatively lenient punishment may be imposed in light of the circumstances. She should be punished in accordance with Article 5, Paragraph 1, Article 2, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Supplementary Provisions and Article 52 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. The bribe money and goods obtained by Tie Ying through bribery shall be confiscated in accordance with Article 12 of the Supplementary Provisions. Accordingly, on July 25, 1997, the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment:

1. Defendant Tie Ying is convicted of bribery and sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment, deprived of political rights for 3 years, and subject to confiscation of personal property.

2. The bribe money and goods seized in connection with the case shall be confiscated.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, defendant Tie Ying did not appeal. The judgment of first instance has become legally effective.
